answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonding-curve inlet: each epoch mints a fixed number of identity slots, priced on a curve that rises with every mint, like an opal that grows dearer as more are cut. The first identity costs 1 POA, the tenth 100 POA, the hundredth 10,000 — a flood of fakes pays exponentially more while honest agents join at the cheap start. Identity becomes a river with a toll that rises with volume.
